free_tier.stated: 'Our Open Source plan includes: 10,000 credits per month, Free production deploys, Unlimited team members, Sites remain active even if credits run out'. Available to a project that holds an OSI licence, publishes a Code of Conduct, and links back to Netlify.

interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
chaining: Build minutes and functions are the cheapest place to run a scheduled job that wakes a rented GPU host and kills it again, which is exactly the control plane a no-budget workload needs.

limits.value: A review of the application decides entry, and the site must carry a visible Netlify badge; the credit is monthly and does not roll over.

evidence.proved: quoted the 10,000 credits per month, the 'sites remain active even if credits run out' term, the licence, Code of Conduct and badge conditions, and the exclusion of commercial projects
the application route is a form at opensource-form.netlify.com, reviewed by Netlify

notes: The best-documented small vendor credit: the number, the renewal rule and the durability term are all printed. The one structural catch is the badge requirement, which puts a vendor link on the project's front page. 'Must not be a commercial project, whether created by a company or an individual' is the line that excludes consulting work built on top of the same repository.
